description: Run ONE SQL statement against a registered foreign Postgres connection (by connection_name) on a WRITE-CAPABLE connection — INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL/anything, not just reads. What the statement is actually allowed to do is decided entirely by the registered credential's own server-side Postgres GRANTs; this verb performs no read/write classification or permission check of its own (vendor RBAC is the control plane, operator ruling 2026-08-09 + Amendment 1). Single-statement contract for v1 (an engineering convention for predictable commit semantics, not a permission gate). A statement with no result set (the common INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL case, no RETURNING) commits and returns rowcount inline. A statement that DOES produce a result set (a RETURNING clause) routes through the same always-TSV export path as run_query — rows are never returned inline, at any size — so output_tsv_path is then required; its absence rolls the whole statement back rather than silently discarding the returned rows while still committing the write. Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) — the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the job finishing. Use list_connections to see registered names.
embedding_description: Write to a registered external Postgres database -- INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL, whatever the credential's own database role permits. Dispatches asynchronously, returning a job_id while the statement commits in the background. A RETURNING clause lands its rows in a workspace TSV, otherwise the rowcount comes back. The one verb that changes data, not just reads it.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the statement's outcome — that arrives separately when the job completes and is delivered as its own message: either {rowcount, has_result_set: false} for a plain write, or {rowcount, has_result_set: true, path, columns, row_count, truncated} when the statement had a RETURNING clause.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued — do not present job_id/status as confirmation the write happened. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the outcome lands in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered: for a plain write, confirm the rowcount affected. For a RETURNING statement, confirm the write AND name the TSV path/row_count/columns like run_query's export (data_sensitivity 0.5 — never inline the file's contents). If the job instead reports an error, do not imply the write partially happened — a failed run_statement job did not commit.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run a SQL statement against a registered foreign Postgres connection on a write-capable connection; the server's own GRANTs decide what it's allowed to do.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: external_pg.invalid_params: missing connection_name/sql, a two-statement sql string, output_tsv_path's parent directory does not exist, the statement produced a result set (RETURNING) but no output_tsv_path was supplied, or acknowledge_default_limit_override/row_limit were not given together / row_limit exceeded the 1000 hard cap. external_pg.export_path_refused: output_tsv_path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry. external_pg.connection_unknown: no connection registered under that name. external_pg.permission_denied: the registered credential's own database role lacks the GRANT for this statement — this is the server's own access decision, not a plugin refusal. external_pg.query_failed: a SQL syntax, constraint, or missing-object error in your statement. external_pg.auth_failed: the registered credential was rejected. external_pg.timeout: the statement exceeded the statement timeout. external_pg.platform_db_refused: the connection targets the platform's own database (refused).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: external_pg.invalid_params naming a RETURNING/missing-path mismatch: either add output_tsv_path or remove the RETURNING clause. external_pg.invalid_params naming two statements: submit exactly one statement per call. external_pg.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root. external_pg.connection_unknown: run list_connections. external_pg.permission_denied: ask the operator to grant the registered credential's database role the needed privilege — this plugin cannot and will not work around a server-side GRANT decision. external_pg.query_failed: fix the SQL. external_pg.timeout: narrow the statement's scope. external_pg.auth_failed: ask the operator to re-check the registered connection.
